feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so I state no outcome for it. The best raced design so far is iteration 1 (score 583.13): the oval finishes 20/20 at 1.97 s, the s-bend finishes 12/20 and the slalom 0/20, with 1.25 line-loss events per run on the slalom. The candidate is valid against the contract: sensor_size 0.016 is an allowed option, mass 0.6 and body_length 0.14 are in range, and line_loss stays 'last_direction'. It changes four things at once: sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016, base_speed 1.3 to 1.2, mass 0.8 to 0.6 and body_length 0.16 to 0.14. Only the sensor change is aimed directly at the line-loss mechanism, so the race will not cleanly separate the effects of the mass and speed changes. Two risks: at 1.2 the s-bend's 2.39 s mean finish time from iteration 1 would scale to roughly 2.6 s, which is still under 3 s but leaves little margin; and 16 mm sensors at 10 mm spacing overlap heavily, so the signal may be less sharp on tight bends. Read the next race this way. If the s-bend finish rate rises above 0.6 and the slalom gets finishes or progress above 0.5, keep this geometry and approach the 3 s limit by nudging base_speed back toward 1.25. If the slalom still goes off track with line_loss_events above 0.5, widen the sensor spread (x = plus or minus 0.03 m, weights scaled to plus or minus 3) before changing kp again. If the oval or s-bend drops in finish rate with steering_oscillation above 0.3, revert mass to 0.8 kg and keep the sensor change.
requested_changes: If the slalom still shows line_loss_events above 0.5 or goes off track: widen controller and geometry sensor spread to x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 m and rescale sensor_weights to -3, -1.5, 0, 1.5, 3, since iteration 1 slalom losses were 1.25 per run with 12 mm sensors.

If completion_time on the s-bend exceeds 2.8 s with finishes: raise controller.base_speed from 1.2 to 1.25 in small steps, keeping kp at 1.5 and kd at 0.6, since iteration 1 s-bend mean finish was 2.39 s at base_speed 1.3.

If steering_oscillation rises above 0.3 on any track after the mass and length change: return geometry.mass to 0.8 and body_length to 0.16 while keeping sensor_size 0.016, to isolate the sensor effect.
